result.verdict: MLX WINS by roughly 3x at both sizes (0.343 and 0.327). MLX is retained.
result.why_we_lose: three separate GPU passes with a full launch each, and one element per thread. MLX does a proper multi-stage reduction with far less launch overhead. Atomics would collapse this to one pass but atomics are still a LARGE gap in the ledger, and borrowing an unbuilt capability to look faster would be a lie about what executes.

an_asymmetry_in_my_own_instrument.defect: compare() measured margin as |speedup - 1|, which is bounded by 100% for ANY slowdown however severe, while a speedup is unbounded. A 3x slowdown scored 67% and was refused; a 3x speedup scored 200% and passed.
an_asymmetry_in_my_own_instrument.consequence: the instrument was quietly HARDER ON LOSSES THAN ON WINS -- exactly the wrong bias for a gate that exists to stop overclaiming. This reduction's 3x loss was being reported as NO_CLAIM.
an_asymmetry_in_my_own_instrument.fix: margin is now max(speedup, 1/speedup) - 1, symmetric by construction
an_asymmetry_in_my_own_instrument.no_prior_verdict_flips: every earlier comparison was re-evaluated under the corrected metric: P5 fusion 1.7081 and 2.6213 still CANDIDATE_WINS, P7 native 2.0796 still CANDIDATE_WINS, GEMM 4096 still BASELINE_WINS at 0.8081, GEMM 1024 still INDISTINGUISHABLE, forge champion still INDISTINGUISHABLE from its runner-up. The fix only ever made losses easier to state.

CORRECTED_BY_LATER_MEASUREMENT.what_was_wrong: 'MLX WINS ~3x' overstated the loss. About half of it was this program's own harness calling mx.eval once per level of the reduction tree, turning one command buffer into three with a host round trip between each.
CORRECTED_BY_LATER_MEASUREMENT.corrected_numbers: With one sync: 0.241 ms vs MLX 0.204 at 2^20 (NO_CLAIM -- margin 18% against 10.6% arm noise) and 0.522 vs 0.298 at 2^24 (MLX wins 1.75x). MLX remains the qualified winner for reduction, by a smaller margin than published.
CORRECTED_BY_LATER_MEASUREMENT.what_still_stands: The correctness results, the load-bearing barrier control (1756.60 -> 1109.53 with the barrier stripped), and the margin-asymmetry fix to compare() -- none of which depended on the sync count.

claim_boundary: A correct f32 sum and max reduction exists in AIR and handles non-power-of-two sizes. It is about 3x slower than MLX and MLX is retained. No scan, no segmented reduction, no other dtype, and no softmax -- so attention remains blocked behind this even though the reduction itself now exists.
